stories.name: wal-tailer-and-broadcaster
stories.title: WAL Tailer and Broadcaster
stories.description: Delivers the core async machinery: an async WAL tailer task, a module-level subscriber registry (set of asyncio.Queue), a ring buffer (deque maxlen=1024), and a broadcast() function that fans events out to all queues. Exposes a Python API (subscribe/unsubscribe, start_tailer/stop_tailer). No HTTP endpoint. Lifespan wiring added to server.py so the tailer starts and stops with the application. Unit-tested by writing lines to a temp WAL file and asserting queues receive correctly structured events.

includes: bridge/events.py — new module with tailer, registry, ring buffer, broadcast()
bridge/server.py _lifespan — wired to start/stop tailer task
bridge/test_events.py — unit tests driving a temp WAL file

test_fixtures.description: Temp WAL file path injected via monkeypatch of _mp._WAL_FILE; existing autouse isolated_palace fixture in conftest.py already provides this
test_fixtures.reason: WAL file lives outside the project; test must redirect to a deterministic temp path

stories.notes: WAL path must be read at call time (str(_mp._WAL_FILE)) not captured at import time, per existing bridge convention. Use asyncio.to_thread for file I/O inside the tailer. Poll interval ~100ms.

stories.name: sse-endpoint-live
stories.title: SSE Endpoint — Live Streaming
stories.description: Adds GET /api/events to server.py using starlette.responses.StreamingResponse. The generator calls subscribe() to get a queue, yields properly framed SSE lines (id:, event:, data:), sends heartbeat comments every 15s, and unsubscribes on disconnect. Tests use TestClient.stream() to open the endpoint while writing to the temp WAL, asserting correct SSE frame structure and heartbeat emission.
stories.notes: Use starlette.responses.StreamingResponse directly (already available via fastapi). Do not add sse_starlette to pyproject.toml. Route handler may be async to use await request.is_disconnected(). Heartbeat via asyncio.wait_for with timeout.

stories.name: resumption-and-filters
stories.title: Resumption and Filters
stories.description: Extends GET /api/events with replay and filtering capabilities: Last-Event-ID header replays from ring buffer (in-memory) or WAL file fallback; ?since_timestamp=<ISO-8601> replays by timestamp; ?ops=<csv> filters by operation; synthetic event: overrun frame emitted when a queue drops the oldest entry on overflow. Tests assert each replay path, filter behaviour, and the overrun event.

includes: bridge/test_events.py — replay tests, filter tests, overrun test
excludes: WAL rotation policy (mempalace does not rotate)
Persistent subscriber state across server restarts

stories.notes: Ring buffer check: if Last-Event-ID >= _ring_buffer[0].id, serve from buffer. Otherwise open _mp._WAL_FILE once and read sequentially. since_timestamp uses >= comparison on ISO-8601 string (lexicographic sort is valid for datetime.now().isoformat() output). ops filter applied after replay and during live streaming.
